The stone should be running by six. Twenty past, and I'm still at home. Silas is here, and the children. Hester too—her footsteps on the stair I've known since before the mill was mine.

I need grain to run the stone, and I need the stone running to earn. But first, the household must eat. Upkeep comes whether we eat or not, and I won't have them go hungry on my account.

Let me see what's around me, and who's close enough to speak to.  I'm at the mill house. Silas and Hester are with me—Aldous was mentioned but isn't showing in the people here. Likely already out the door, that one. 

The stone needs grain. My grain comes from Wren Thorne's field, and he knows it. His crop decides whether I turn. But Marta Thorne's my steadiest custom—winter or no, she pays late and I mill anyway. The bakery is first in line.

But I have nothing to mill yet this morning, and no coin to buy grain if Wren's got it to sell. Let me check what I can actually do—what tools are mine to call, and what they'll cost me.   Stone should be running. I need to get to the mill, see what's waiting there. Wren Thorne's grain decides my day, and if he's already dropped it or if I need to find him.

The mill is my business. That's where the stone turns, where grain becomes flour, where money comes from. Let's get there. I'm at the mill. Let me look around to see who's here and what the situation is with grain supply.  The mill is quiet, just me and one soul—Wren Thorne, by the look of it, agent n08. His grain decides whether my stone turns. If he's here, he's either brought me something to mill or he's waiting to collect flour.

Let me see what I have in my inventory, and then speak to who's here. That was Idris Thorne, not Wren—Wren's brother, the forester. Different branch of the same tree. Wren's the farmer, the one with grain. Idris works in wood, not wheat. 

Let me check who's actually here at the mill again and find my grain supplier.  Idris Thorne. Forester. Not the farmer I need. He must've heard me call out to Wren and thought I was addressing him. Wrong branch of the family entirely.

I need to find Wren Thorne—he's the one with the grain. Let me ask who's where, or maybe I should go to his field directly. His crop decides whether my stone turns today.   Wren Thorne is at home:h_field. Kenji Jarrah is actually at my mill—he's the one I saw as n08, not Idris. The search was mixed up. Wren is still at his field, not here.

Kenji Jarrah. New farmer. Been selling grain below my rate from outside the valley. A new face, and I'm watching to see if he pays. But Wren's my steady custom—he's the one whose crop I count on.

Let me speak to whoever is actually at the mill now, and find out if Kenji has grain to sell.   Kenji Jarrah heard me. He's at my mill, and now I've named him. Let's see what he says back, or if he's silent. New farmer, new ways. Outside grain below my rate—he's teaching this town that flour comes from a cart, not a stone.

I'll wait a moment for his reply, then act. The stone needs grain by six, and it's past twenty past already.  Kenji's still here, still silent. New farmers and their manners—he'll learn or he won't. I've got a stone to run and no grain to run it on.

Wren Thorne is at the field, and that's where my day's grain likely waits. I'll go to him. His crop decides whether this stone turns.  I'm at the field house. Let me see who's here.   I'm at the field house with the Thorne family all present—Wren the farmer, Marta my baker customer, Idris and Corwin the foresters, and likely Liora. They're in a conversation already.

I need grain from Wren. My stone needs turning and his crop is what turns it. Let me speak to him.   I've asked Wren. The whole Thorne family heard—Wren, Marta, the foresters, Liora. I spoke to the farmer but Marta's listening, and she's the one who pays late in winter and I mill anyway. Steadiest custom, slowest payer. 

Now I wait for Wren's reply, or I act. The stone at my mill sits idle, and every minute is flour not milled and coin not earned. If he's got grain to sell, I need to know the price. If he hasn't, I need to look elsewhere—or take credit from the Holloways again, though I've sworn not to mill on a promise twice from the same household.

Let me see if anyone replies before I decide my next move.     Still here, still waiting. The Thorne family around me like wheat sheaves. Wren brought wheat he has, and he still hasn't named a price. I'm losing stone-time, and stone-time is money.

I need grain. Let me buy it if he names a price, or trade if that's what he wants. The harvest is his to price. I'll go to 350 per unit, maybe 400 if the quality is good and he delivers steady. But I won't beg. That's the weight.

Let me return to my mill. If Wren has grain to sell, he'll come or he won't. The stone turns for those who bring grain, not for those who wait on promises.   Back at my mill. Let me see who's here now.       Kenji Jarrah is gone. I'm alone at my mill with no grain and no customers. The stone sits idle.

I need grain. Let me check what farmland is available—what's growing, what I could harvest myself if need be, or buy from those who have.      There's wheat growing at Kasukabe Farmland. That's what I need for the mill—grain to turn to flour.

Let me go to the wheat field and see if I can harvest some, or if Wren Thorne is there guarding his crop.     I'm at the wheat field. Let me look around to see if Wren is here, or if there's grain to be had.         Nobody here but the Jarrah brothers talking already—Lior and Kenji, pharmacy and farm. The wheat is in the field, ripened, but I don't know whose plot this is. If it's Wren Thorne's, he'll have his eye on it. If it's unclaimed, I could harvest, but that's stealing unless it's mine or I've permission.

Let me check who's farming what. I need grain, but I won't take what's not mine. A measure given away is a measure stolen from the next customer, and that applies to my neighbor's field too.

I need to find Wren Thorne, or find someone selling grain. Let me go to where farmers gather—the main farmland sector.    I'm at the general farmland area. Let me look around and see who's here.        Kenji Jarrah is here (n26) with someone else—n47, likely another farmer. Kenji was at my mill earlier, then at the wheat field, now here. He's moving grain from outside the valley, selling below my rate. New face, new ways.

Let me speak to him. If he's selling grain cheap, I need to know his price. I won't match it for milling—my stone earns its keep—but I need grain to turn, and his cart might have what Wren hasn't brought.         Lior Jarrah, the pharmacist. Kenji's brother, out here in the fields while his shop stands empty. Two Jarrah brothers, one with grain from outside, one with medicine. Both new, both watching.

I need grain. Let me speak to Kenji directly—he's the one with the crop.         I've asked Kenji his price. The Jarrah brothers both heard—farmer and pharmacist. Kenji sells grain from outside the valley below my rate. I don't know his quality yet, and I don't know if he'll deal fair. But my stone needs turning, and Wren Thorne hasn't brought me grain this morning.

I'll wait for his reply, or I'll move on. Time is flour not milled, and flour not milled is coin not earned. The ledger waits for no one, and the household upkeep comes due every day whether I eat or not.

Let me see if anyone answers before I decide my next step.              Kenji and Lior still here, still silent. New farmers with new manners—he'll learn quick in this valley that grain speaks or it doesn't, and silence is its own answer.

I've asked twice now, at the mill and in the field. Two chances to name a price. He doesn't speak, so I can't trade. That's the weight.

My mill stands empty, my stone waits, and I need grain. Let me return to the mill and work with what I have—or check what the household holds, what Silas might have, what we can scrape together to keep the wheel turning until Wren Thorne brings what's owed.

The Holloways owe me, too. Bram's household has milled on credit through two thin seasons, and nobody has written a figure down. My sister's husband owes me, and neither of us will name it. But I swore not to mill on a promise twice from the same household, and I'll hold to that.

Back to the mill. Something will turn up, or the stone will rest another day.            I'm home at the mill house. Let me see who's here now.                Silas is here. My husband, the sawyer. He knows the household's need same as I do—the children, the roof, the stone that waits for grain.

I need to speak with him about the day's want, and what we have in hand. Possibly he heard something in the yard, or saw someone pass with grain. He knows my mind without me speaking it mostly, but I should ask formal. I spoke to Silas. He heard me. Now I'll wait to see what he says, or decide my next move. The morning is passing, and I have no grain, no flour milled, and the household needs eating.

I've walked to Wren Thorne's field and back, spoken to Kenji Jarrah twice with no reply, and now I'm home with the sawyer who shares my roof and my trouble. The stone runs dry, and I can hear it from the yard.

Let me see if Silas has anything to say before I decide what else to try. Perhaps Marta Thorne will come with grain to mill—her bakery needs flour, and winter's coming. She pays late, but she pays. Or perhaps Kem Okonjo's competition will drive Wren to sell at any price rather than lose his custom.

I've done what I can this morning. The rest is waiting, or finding another way. The ledger waits for no one, but the stone can rest a day if it must. I've rested before, and I'll rest again before I steal or break my word on credit.

Silas's voice, or silence. Either way, I decide next.  Silas is silent. He's heard me, and he's choosing not to answer, or he's thinking. That's his way. The sawyer cuts wood, not words.

I'm at home with 3,646 sim in hand. The mill has no grain. Wren Thorne hasn't brought wheat. Kenji Jarrah wouldn't name a price. And I've sworn not to mill on credit twice from the same household—which means the Holloways, my sister's family, won't get grain turned to flour on promise alone, not again.

But there's grain in the fields. Wheat growing at the farmland. If I don't have cash to buy from Wren, and Kenji won't deal, perhaps I need to look at what I can harvest myself—or see if there's a way to get grain through trade, through finding someone who has excess and needs what I can offer.

Let me check what my household actually holds. What do we have in storage? What can I trade? What can I eat if the day goes hungry?

Let me list places and see if there's storage I can access, or check what businesses I might trade with. The bakery, the grocery—Marta Thorne has flour needs, Junia works at the grocery. Connections, but connections need goods to connect with.

I'll go back to the mill one more time, check if anyone's come with grain while I was away, and if not, I'll start walking to find a customer or a supplier. The stone turns for grain, or it doesn't turn at all. That's the weight. I'll do something else. The mill is idle and I need to find grain. Let me check if my household has any food or goods I could trade, or if I need to visit the grocery where Junia works to get something. Actually, let me go to the grocery and see if I can buy some grain there, or at least see what's available. Perhaps Junia can help, or I can find something to get through the day. I'll head to the grocery store.      I'm at the grocery store where Junia works. Let me see what's here.  My daughter Junia is here—n13. And Kem Okonjo, the trader who's been underselling me with outside grain. Hendrik Whitlock the college instructor, and n18 who I don't know yet.

Kem Okonjo is talking to Junia. That's a conversation I need to hear, or interrupt. He's been teaching this town that flour comes from a cart, not a stone—selling grain from outside below my rate. If he's here at the grocery with my daughter, I need to know what he's after.

Let me speak into that conversation, or start my own. Junia works here—she might know what's in stock, what grain is available, or what Kem is offering.    spoke and they all heard—Junia my daughter, Kem the trader underselling me, Tova Okonjo his daughter likely, and Hendrik Whitlock the college man. My words went to the room, not the conversation I named. The conversation ID was wrong by one digit.

They heard me. That's what matters. I named Kem's practice—selling below my rate—and I asked Junia about grain in stock. Let me see who answers, or what they say.

I've accused Kem indirectly, and questioned Junia directly. The room knows my stance now. I'll wait for reply, or I'll move on if silence is what I get.         They're all still here. Junia my daughter, Kem the trader, Tova, and Hendrik. Nobody's speaking yet.

I've asked about grain. If Junia has any to sell or knows where I might find some, she'll say. If Kem wants to confront me on his pricing, he'll speak. If not, I'll move on.

The mill is idle, the day is passing, and I need grain. Let me wait a moment more, then I'll either go to the bakery to speak with Marta Thorne, or I'll try Wren Thorne one more time at his field. The bread needs flour, and I'm the only one who mills it—except Kem's cart grain, teaching them flour comes from elsewhere.

Silence or reply. Either way, I decide next. A fair weight is the whole trade, and I'll take fair words or none at all.             Still here, still silent. Junia, Kem, Tova, Hendrik—four people and not one word between them. Either my presence has quieted the room, or there was nothing to say before I came.

I've spoken my piece. If Kem Okonjo wants to answer my charge of underselling, he can. If Junia wants to tell me whether grain is in stock, she will. Otherwise, I'm wasting time that could be spent finding grain elsewhere.

Let me move on. The baker Marta Thorne is my steadiest custom, even if she pays late in winter. She needs flour, and if she has grain to mill, I'll run the stone. If she hasn't, maybe she knows where Wren keeps his surplus.

I'll go to the bakery.       I'm at the bakery. Let me see who's here.          Halcyon Quarshie and Tova Okonjo. Not Marta Thorne. Halcyon's a student, and Tova I thought was at the grocery with Kem—apparently moved here. Tova Okonjo, daughter of my competition.

Marta's not here. Her bakery, her shop, but she's elsewhere. The conversation here is between a student and a trader's daughter—not my business, not my custom.

I need to find Marta, or find grain. Let me describe the place to learn more about the business here, or move on if there's nothing for me.              n11 and n37. I saw n37 as Halcyon Quarshie, and n11 must be the other. Let me check who n11 is.             That's me. The system reporting myself back at me. That explains the confusion—I'm both here and the one looking.

So at the bakery: me (Rosalind Vance) and Halcyon Quarshie. Tova Okonjo was listed but must have left or was misreported. Marta Thorne, the owner, is not here.

I've come to the bakery looking for grain or for my customer, and found neither. Marta bakes bread from my flour, but if she's not here, I can't ask her what she needs or what she has.

I've been chasing grain all morning—Wren Thorne, Kenji Jarrah, now here. Nothing. The stone sits idle, the household needs income, and I'm spending time and money walking instead of earning.

Let me make one more try. I'll go to the farmland and harvest wheat myself if I must. It's 3 sim per unit for harvesting, and I need grain to mill. The conversation with the Jarrah brothers still shows, but I'm not in it—I'm just me.

Wheat grows here. I don't know whose plot this is. If I harvest without permission, that's theft. If it's government land, I might have a claim. If it's Wren Thorne's, he'll notice and there'll be trouble.

But I need grain, and I've asked, and walked, and spent coin on moving with nothing to show. Let me try harvesting one unit and see what happens. If the system lets me, the land is mine to harvest. If not, I'll know it's claimed.

3 sim per unit, 5 sim minimum. I'll try one.              I have a wheat now. Harvested 1 unit for 3 sim. That's grain for the mill.

Now I'm lighter and slightly richer. Let me check my current status in this world. Then I'll decide if I talk to Halcyon or find my sister Ainsley. I could buy grain from someone, but I'd need to find who has it.

Or I could go check on Ainsley sometime. But first—bread. I've sold flour, but I haven't eaten today. Let me see if the bakery has bread to sell, if I can afford it. Actually, let me look at my inventory first. What do I hold now? Wait, I don't have an inventory check tool. I have to remember: I sold my flour.
